package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical vulnerability (CVE-2017-5638) in its multipart file upload handling, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary system commands on the server by sending specially crafted HTTP requests. This enables remote code execution (RCE) and has been actively exploited in the wild, leading to major data breaches.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: buildErrorMessage function processes Content-Type header in a way that allows injected OGNL expressions to be evaluated, e.g. Content-Type: %{(#_='multipart/form-data').(#dm=@ognl.OgnlContext@DEFAULT_MEMBER_ACCESS)...}
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Processes the Content-Type header of incoming multipart/form-data requests. If the header contains a specially crafted OGNL expression, the code evaluates it, allowing arbitrary code execution on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Evaluating user-supplied data (HTTP headers) as code is highly dangerous and almost always a sign of a vulnerability or backdoor.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to treat Content-Type as a static string, not as executable code. Here, user input is evaluated as OGNL, breaking the security boundary.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: OGNL expressions are used for data binding in Struts, but never intended to be evaluated from untrusted HTTP headers.
key_indicators: OGNL expression evaluation from HTTP headers
No sanitization or validation of Content-Type header
Ability to execute arbitrary system commands via crafted requests

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request with a malicious Content-Type header containing an OGNL expression.
attack_chain.leads_to: OGNL expression is evaluated by the vulnerable Struts2 code.

attack_chain.action: The OGNL expression is executed in the context of the web server process, allowing arbitrary code execution (e.g., running system commands, dropping web shells, exfiltrating data).
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote code execution on the server, leading to data breaches or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected system command execution triggered by HTTP requests
OGNL expressions present in HTTP headers (especially Content-Type)
Unusual error messages or stack traces referencing OGNL or multipart parsing
network_indicators: HTTP requests with Content-Type headers containing OGNL expressions (e.g., %{...})
Outbound connections from the web server to attacker-controlled infrastructure following exploitation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP traffic for Content-Type headers containing OGNL expressions (e.g., %{...}). Inspect server logs for errors or stack traces referencing multipart parsing or OGNL evaluation. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes to web application files. Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by the web server process. Upgrade Struts2 to a non-vulnerable version and/or switch to a different multipart parser.
